_note: Which medicines in this formulary are commonly considered for which symptom after concussion. This is not a ranking and it is not advice. It is the ordinary clinical association between a symptom and a class of medicine, so a clinician looking at a symptom score has somewhere to start reading rather than scrolling the whole formulary.
_never: No doses anywhere. The words recommend and best are not used, because the model has no standing to say either and a list that used them would read as prescribing.
_evidence_tags: verified means the source was fetched and read. check this means the association is written from general clinical knowledge and the named source still has to be read end to end before anybody leans on it. The VA/DoD and AAN documents below are real and current, and their URLs are here, but their PDFs could not be text extracted when this file was written, so the per symptom claims drawn from them are tagged check this rather than verified.

vadod2021.text: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management and Rehabilitation of Post-Acute Mild Traumatic Brain Injury, 2021, version 3.0

cdc_heads_up.text: CDC, Heads Up, concussion symptom management

aan2013.text: American Academy of Neurology, Summary of evidence-based guideline update: evaluation and management of concussion in sports, Neurology 2013;80(24):2250-2257

_threshold_note: A symptom is counted as reported when its score is 4 or more out of 10. Fixed rather than relative, so the same score means the same thing for every patient and two weeks can be compared.

drugs.name: acetaminophen
drugs.why: a first line simple analgesic for headache

drugs.name: ibuprofen
drugs.why: a first line anti-inflammatory for headache

drugs.name: amitriptyline
drugs.why: used at low dose for frequent post-traumatic headache

drugs.name: nortriptyline
drugs.why: an alternative where amitriptyline is too sedating

drugs.name: propranolol
drugs.why: used to prevent migraine-type headache

drugs.name: gabapentin
drugs.why: sometimes used for persistent headache

drugs.name: ondansetron
drugs.why: a standard antiemetic, used for nausea from any cause

drugs.name: melatonin
drugs.why: used for sleep timing after concussion and generally well tolerated

drugs.name: amitriptyline
drugs.why: sedating, so sometimes used where headache and poor sleep occur together

drugs.name: gabapentin
drugs.why: sometimes used where pain is keeping sleep broken

drugs.name: sertraline
drugs.why: a first line SSRI for mood and anxiety symptoms

drugs.name: propranolol
drugs.why: used for the physical symptoms of anxiety

drugs.name: amitriptyline
drugs.why: an older antidepressant, more often used here for headache and sleep

drugs.name: methylphenidate
drugs.why: studied for attention and processing speed after TBI, mostly in moderate to severe injury

drugs.name: amantadine
drugs.why: studied after TBI, though the main trial was in severe injury with disorders of consciousness, not concussion

drugs.name: methylphenidate
drugs.why: sometimes used for fatigue and low arousal after TBI

drugs.name: amantadine
drugs.why: sometimes used for fatigue after TBI

drugs.name: melatonin
drugs.why: used where fatigue is being driven by broken sleep

dizziness.label: Dizziness

drugs.name: ondansetron
drugs.why: used where dizziness comes with nausea

dizziness.note: The guidelines put vestibular rehabilitation ahead of medicine for dizziness after concussion.

light_sensitivity.label: Light or noise sensitivity

drugs.name: amitriptyline
drugs.why: used where light sensitivity travels with frequent headache

light_sensitivity.note: Usually managed by pacing and gradual exposure rather than by medicine.
